standard_prerequisites.name: The Artin-Rees consequence supplies a constant c such that the kernels and cokernels of the comparison maps between Hom(M, N) modulo I^n and Hom(M_n, N_n) are killed by I^c
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 29094-29098 and used at proof lines 28999-29101
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces both the constant of part (2) and the Mittag-Leffler property of part (1).

standard_prerequisites.name: For finite modules over a Noetherian ring the completions satisfy M over I^n equal to M-completion over I^n times the completion, and Hom between the completions is the inverse limit of the Hom groups of the quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the identification of the limit of the Hom systems with the group of homomorphisms between the completions, which is part (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma and the resulting surjectivity criterion for endomorphisms of finite modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the maps alpha and beta in the final argument are isomorphisms, which yields part (4) for the systems of isomorphisms.

core_obligations: Rewrite Hom_A(M_n, N_n) as Hom_A(M, N_n), choose a presentation of M and apply the right exact functor Hom_A(-, N) to obtain the two-term complex whose middle cohomology is Hom_A(M, N) and whose reduction modulo I^n computes Hom_A(M_n, N_n) (proof lines 29081-29094).

Choose the constant c supplied by the Artin-Rees consequence for this presentation and deduce from part (3) of that consequence the Mittag-Leffler property of the system (Hom_A(M_n, N_n)) (proof lines 29094-29098).

Read off that the kernels and cokernels of Hom_A(M, N) over I^n Hom_A(M, N) to Hom_A(M_n, N_n) are killed by I^c, and use part (2) of the consequence to identify the inverse limit with the I-adic completion of Hom_A(M, N) (proof lines 29099-29103).
Identify the completion of Hom_A(M, N) with Hom between the completed modules using that M over I^n equals the completion modulo I^n and the corresponding statement for N (proof lines 29103-29109).

Handle isomorphisms: apply the result for homomorphisms to both the (M_n, N_n) and the (N_n, M_n) systems, and use Nakayama together with the surjectivity criterion to conclude that maps alpha and beta inducing isomorphisms modulo I^m for some m greater than n are themselves isomorphisms (proof lines 29111-29120).
proof_roadmap: Present M by free modules and dualize to get two-term complexes whose cohomology computes the Hom groups at every level (proof lines 29081-29094).
Import the Artin-Rees constant, get Mittag-Leffler and the bounded kernels and cokernels, and identify the limit with the completion of Hom (proof lines 29094-29103).
Identify that completion with Hom between the completed modules (proof lines 29103-29109).
Deduce the statement for isomorphisms from the homomorphism case plus Nakayama and the surjectivity criterion (proof lines 29111-29120).
difficulty_reason: The statement collects four facts about the systems obtained by reducing Hom and Isom groups modulo powers of an ideal: the Mittag-Leffler property, a uniform bound on the kernels and cokernels of the comparison maps, and the identification of the limits with Hom and Isom between the completed modules (statement lines 29059-29078). The proof replaces the Hom groups by the cohomology of a two-term complex obtained by dualizing a presentation of M, imports the Artin-Rees constant to get the Mittag-Leffler property and the uniform bound, and then identifies the limit with the completion of Hom, which is where the completeness of the completions is used (proof lines 29081-29109). The final part transfers the result to isomorphisms by applying the homomorphism case twice and invoking Nakayama, so the four assertions are proved in one coherent argument. The counted span refers four times, three of them to labelled results of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs; the complexes, the limits and the isomorphism argument are inside the span.
